Draws 32 SU per RPM while active (2048/4096/8192 SU at the tier floors) and takes 16s to heat at each floor; overshoot the RPM to heat faster at a higher cost. The Induction Coil is the fuel for Kindled and Superheated and wears as it runs (Kindled about a third the rate); with no coil the plate only idles at passive Warm. Hoppers can restock the slot. The plate bulk-cooks any campfire recipe at 1x Warm, 2x Kindled or 3.3x Superheated, and nothing is ever flung on the floor; your steak waits for you.

block.create_stats.power_distribution_un: Serves its branch by priority and sheds what it cannot power.

Nine outputs. Run a Copper Wire from any of the eight studs on the top bus bar to a machine's Power Connector, or lay cable on the boss at the back for the ninth. Each is its own leg with its own breaker. Feed FE in through either side boss.

Three modes. Off shares power evenly. Manual serves Critical first and works down, shedding the tiers it cannot reach. Active Auto measures what your generators actually produce and runs the most important set that supply can sustain.

A shed device coasts on its own reserve and reads amber LOAD SHED, not red NO POWER. Right-click a row to lock a machine on so it is never shed, or off so it never runs. Tunable in [power.pdu] and [power.pdu.auto].

Grids serve machines before storage, so a bank charges from surplus and discharges only to cover a real shortfall. Capacity and rate are tunable in the [power.storage] config.

create_stats.manual.page.intro.body: This manual gives the quick version. Pick a page on the left to see what a block does, how to use it, and when it helps. If a page spans more than one sheet, use the arrows on the right page to flip through the rest. Sincerely, HEB.
create_stats.manual.page.stats_display_p: The Stats Display Panel is a wall-mounted display for live factory data. Right-click it to open the panel UI and view the current graph or dashboard; sneak-right-click to cycle the display mode. When multiple panels face the same direction, they can form a larger multiblock display with one controller. Use a Stats Configurator to copy or paste settings, and hold Shift while placing panels to auto-fill matching neighbors when you want to build a larger screen quickly.
create_stats.manual.page.stats_configura: The Stats Configurator is the tuning tool for Create Stats displays and alarms. Use it on a Stats Display Panel to open settings, or sneak-use it on a panel to copy that panel's layout into the tool. Use the charged Configurator on another panel to paste the layout there. It also opens settings for Stats Alarms, Status Tower Lights, and Holographic Projectors, making it the item you reach for when a display is showing the right data but needs different colors, radius, thresholds, or presentation.
The Stats Handheld is a pocket terminal for live and stored readouts. Use it on a Stats Display Panel, Stats Recorder, or Dispatch Board to link a remote view, then right-click in the air to open the handheld screen. Mounted signal antennas on the linked target extend same-dimension reach, and TRT targets can bridge loaded Overworld and Nether links. It can show live graphs from linked targets and report when the link is missing, out of range, or in another dimension. Hold a filled Memory Cog in the other hand to inspect a local snapshot instead. Sneak-right-click in the air to clear the current remote link.
create_stats.manual.page.memory_cog.body: The Memory Cog is portable storage for recorded stats. Use an empty cog on a Stats Recorder after it has samples to write a snapshot into the cog. Filled cogs glint and show their metric type, sample count, source, position, and dimension in the tooltip when that information is available. Hold a filled cog in the off hand while opening the Stats Handheld to replay the stored graph away from the machine that produced it.
create_stats.manual.page.signal_antennas: Signal Antennas mount on compatible Create Stats blocks to extend direct reach without turning the system into a chunk loader. Small antennas give 4x same-dimension direct reach. Advanced antennas give 12x same-dimension direct reach. TRT antennas are the special tier: they allow loaded Overworld and Nether direct links and also give unlimited same-dimension direct reach in those two realms. Right-click a compatible block to mount one, or sneak-right-click the mounted block with a wrench or empty hand to remove it. For Display Links and Stats Handheld reads, the target block's antenna is the important one; for Factory Logic Controller clutch links, the controller itself needs TRT. Some blocks also use antennas to widen capped local scans, such as alarms, projectors, and recorders. Antennas do not load chunks.
create_stats.manual.page.aero_stats_link: Create Aeronautics compatibility is treated as an integration layer. When a compatible Aeronautics build is present, supported airship or flight blocks can expose telemetry through Create's Display Link flow and into Create Stats targets such as panels, recorders, dials, lights, and projectors. This entry is a placeholder until the exact Aeronautics source names are locked in; trust the Display Link source list in-game over any old wording from earlier drafts.
create_stats.manual.page.aero_source_mat: The idea is simple: motion, attitude, lift, propulsion, docking, and navigation data should be readable by the Create Stats instrument network when the matching Aeronautics block exposes that data. To extract the data you MUST choose "Stats Link" in the display link interface.
create_stats.manual.page.contraption_inf: Airship readiness is depends on the type, you will have 3 special modes. Contraption Info and Aerodeck apears and starts working ONLY after connecting a gimbal sensor. However, for AEROLINE you need to enrich it with Navigation Table from Aeronautics. All the other sensors are still needed but not mandatory
create_stats.manual.page.aero_flight_dec: Nickname "Aerodeck". Its job is to collect the currently available airship telemetry into one readable operator view, then let specialized pages handle the details. Try to see the differences from Aeroline and Contraption info
create_stats.manual.page.aeroline_direct: Aeroline Director is for a guidance-style Create Aeronautics display. It will act as your GPS. While Aerodeck also shows you the info this one priotize the target location.
create_stats.manual.page.hot_air_burner_: Well gives you the info in a more standard way. Nothing fancy just the DATAAA
create_stats.manual.page.calculator.body: The Calculator is a compact math block for quick counting and graphing. Press the face buttons to build an expression, use C or backspace to edit, and click the display to open the full calculator screen. It keeps your current expression, shows the latest result or error, and stores recent calculations. Sneak-placing a matching Calculator can auto-fill a 2x3 panel, and Scientific mode unlocks x, powers, pi/e, and functions for graphing and advanced formulas.
The Stats Recorder is the capture box for your factory instruments. It can still record data sent in from a Display Link, but it also arms itself when placed near a Stats Display and mirrors that panel's main channel automatically. Right-click with an empty hand to see whether it is armed, recording, paused, or waiting for a source. Hold an empty Memory Cog and interact with the recorder to copy the stored samples into a portable snapshot.
create_stats.manual.page.production_dete: Visual Inventory Display lesson. Use the sheet arrows to step through the diagrams.
create_stats.manual.page.flow_meter.body: The Flow Meter is like a speed sign for your fluid pipes. Put it in the middle of a pumped pipe and the fluid flows straight through, just like a normal pipe, while the meter counts how fast it moves. Point a Display Link from the meter at a Stats Display to see the flow speed in mB per tick, which fluid it is, which way it goes, and the total moved so far. Switch the panel to Specialized mode for an animated pipe with a flow gauge and a direction arrow, plus an Alarm and Redstone Trigger you can set to fire while fluid is Flowing or when the Amount passes a number you pick, powering both the display panel and the meter pipe. Tip: if the tank in front is full the fluid cannot move, so the meter correctly reads Idle even while a pump keeps pushing. Use the sheet arrows to step through the diagrams.
create_stats.manual.page.stats_alarm.bod: Place the Stats Alarm near a Stats Display Panel controller to watch your network for trouble. It scans nearby panels for any active channel that reaches its alert threshold, then turns on, plays a configurable sound, can spawn particles, and may show a warning message. Use the Stats Configurator to adjust scan radius, sound, visibility, and whether the alarm also powers redstone.
create_stats.manual.page.table_alarm_clo: The Alarm Clock is a small wooden desk clock for simple time jobs. Put it on a table, shelf, or control desk, then right-click it to open the clock screen. Clock mode shows the current game time. Stopwatch mode lets you start, stop, and reset a timer for counting how long something takes. Timer mode counts down from the time you set. Alarm mode rings every day at the game time you choose. When the timer or alarm finishes, the clock rings, lights up, and sends redstone until you silence it.
create_stats.manual.page.status_tower_li: The Status Tower Light is a compact operator lamp for machine status. Place it above a compatible machine for local monitoring, or link it to a remote source with a Display Link. Configure it with right-click to choose the source mode, metric, and whether the light uses warning thresholds or simple on-off logic. Green means normal, yellow means warning or no data, and red means critical; the critical state also emits redstone power.
create_stats.manual.page.data_dial.body: The Data Dial is a wall-mounted gauge for live machine readouts. Place it against a sturdy face to read the block behind it in Local mode, or switch it to Linked mode to follow values sent in from a Display Link. Right-click cycles the metric being shown, and sneak-right-click swaps the mode. The needle and comparator output both follow the selected reading, so it works as both a visual dial and a compact analog signal source.
create_stats.manual.page.factory_logic_c: The Factory Logic Controller stops a branch when its machines sit idle for too long. Each row needs a Machine Selection Card for the watched area and a Clutch Link Card for the branch clutch. Set the idle time with the +/- buttons. Pause keeps a row off until Reset. When work resumes, the controller sends RUN again. It is built for Control Clutches, and works best with presses and mixers. Mount a TRT Signal Antenna on the controller itself if you want loaded Overworld and Nether clutch links; normal antennas only affect local reach.
create_stats.manual.page.machine_selecti: Use the Machine Selection Card to tell one controller row what to watch. Sneak-right-click a machine to store its type. Then click two positions in the same dimension to mark the watched area. Using the card again after both corners are set starts a new selection. Hold the card to preview the hovered machine or saved box. Put it in the same controller row as the matching Clutch Link Card.
create_stats.manual.page.safety_clutch_l: Use the Kinetic Control Card to tell one controller row what it commands. Right-click a Control Clutch or a Kinetic Flywheel to store its position, then place the card in a controller row. A clutch row also needs a Machine Selection Card; a flywheel row stands alone. Sneak-right-click in the air to clear the link. For several flywheels on one shaft network, use the controller's Bank toggle: Parallel shares the load, Sequential runs one at a time, and Smart holds a target RPM.
create_stats.manual.page.mini_display.bo: The Mini Display is a compact wall-mounted readout for machine stats. Place it on a sturdy face to read the machine beneath it, or switch it to linked mode to relay a Display Link source instead. It can show item storage, fluids, boiler info, and kinetic data, and two Mini Displays placed side by side merge into a wider 2x1 display. Right-click it to configure what it tracks, and for item storage you can hold a filter item while configuring to pin a specific item.
create_stats.manual.page.holographic_pro: The Holographic Projector is a central stats display for your factory. Feed it data with a Display Link, or enable the nearby scanner to pick up supported blocks like gauges, tanks, switches, and stations around it. It renders the selected channels as floating holograms, can be tuned with the Stats Configurator, and can also emit redstone based on a chosen channel. Place it on a solid block in a control room or dashboard area where you want live readouts at a glance.
create_stats.manual.page.safety_clutch.b: The Safety Clutch is a kinetic safety valve for Create networks. Place it inline on a shaft line to monitor the stress flowing through that network. When the network reaches its set stress threshold, or goes into overload, the clutch trips and cuts power to protect the machinery downstream. Open its settings with right-click to choose the trip threshold, hysteresis, and whether it stays latched or automatically resets after the load drops. Use it anywhere you want a machine line to fail safe instead of burning out under pressure.
create_stats.manual.page.auto_transmissi: Place the Auto Variable Clutch inline on a kinetic line to turn it into an automatic stress governor. Open its UI to set a stress band in SU or percent and define min and max RPM, then connect it between a power source and your machines. The clutch watches the network and changes ratio on its own: it speeds up when stress is below target and slows down when stress rises above it. If the network drops out, it holds neutral until power returns.
The Control Clutch is the branch clutch for the Factory Logic Controller. Place it in the shaft line you want a controller row to stop or restart. Link it with a Clutch Link Card, then insert that card into the controller. The clutch does not tune stress or speed on its own. It only follows RUN and STOP from its linked row. Right-click for link details, and use the comparator or redstone output when you need status outside the menu.
create_stats.manual.page.load_balancer.b: The Load Balancer is a split-shaft kinetic block for dividing one driven shaft into two output lines. Place it so the rear face receives power; the left and right faces feed the two branches, and right-click to open its controls. Set a stress band, choose how the load is split, and pick Strict or Elastic sharing. In Strict mode each branch follows its own share; in Elastic mode it can borrow extra headroom when one side needs more. The block reports when the input is missing, the topology is invalid, or the branches have been merged.
create_stats.manual.page.smart_gearshift: Smart Gearshift is a redstone preset gearbox for kinetic shafts. Each redstone level from 0 to 15 selects a speed stage: level 0 passes input through, while higher levels convert the incoming rotation to one of 15 target RPMs from 8 up to 256. It can boost or throttle to reach the chosen stage, but it never exceeds 256 RPM. Place it inline on a kinetic line and power it with redstone to change speeds on the fly. A Display Link can show the current stage, target RPM, source RPM, and whether the block is boosting or throttling.
create_stats.manual.page.overflow_gate.b: The Overflow Gate is a belt splitter for Create logistics. Place it above a moving belt to sort one buffered stack across the three side outputs around the belt. It sends items to matching filtered sides first, then to any open side, and only then to the chosen overflow side, so you can keep a main line moving while diverting extra items where you want them. Right-click to check its current routing, and sneak-right-click to take back anything waiting in the buffer.
create_stats.manual.page.kinetic_flywhee: The Kinetic Flywheel is a kinetic stress battery, an Inertia Bank that stores surplus capacity and gives it back when the network runs short. Place it inline on a shaft: while the network has spare stress it charges and banks the energy, and when the network falls short it becomes a source on its own and drives up to 32,768 SU at 256 RPM, with the speed sagging gently as the reserve drains. A base bank holds about 3.27M SU-seconds, roughly 90 seconds at full output, at 90% round-trip efficiency. Stack up to three extra Create flywheels on top to raise the mass stage from x1 to x4, scaling output and reserve together. The charge gear sets how fast it fills (180, 90, or 60 seconds) while the discharge gear sets how hard it pushes (about 90, 45, or 30 seconds of sustain). If the network overloads, it trips for safety and re-arms after a moment for a small slice of reserve. Wear engineer's goggles to read the Inertia Bank panel, or use the comparator output or a Display Link to follow charge level, mode, output, and remaining sustain.
create_stats.manual.page.freight_manifes: The Freight Manifest Clipboard is a station-linked notice board for train cargo planning. First right-click a Create station with the clipboard item to bind it to that station, then place the block standing on the ground or mounted on a wall. Once linked, right-click the clipboard to open the station's freight manifest and manage the cargo checklist for that route. You can also use a linked clipboard item to relink the placed block or copy the block's link back into your hand.
The Dispatch Board is a public operations display for a freight station. First right-click a Create station with the board item to bind it, then place it standing on the ground or mounted on a wall near the linked platform. Right-click the placed board to open the live dispatch screen. The board shows cargo totals, delivery-order status, and train presence at a glance. Operators with permission can hide, reveal, or reset delivery orders from the board, while the Freight Manifest Clipboard remains the tool for full manifest authoring. You can also sneak-right-click a placed board with a linked clipboard to relink it or copy the board link back into the clipboard item.

create_stats.manual.page.rpm_governor.bo: This block is the FCC's hand on a shaft. Put one RPM Governor on each shaft you want the FCC to control. Then open the Flight Control Computer and bind that Governor to the right device. If the FCC stops talking, the Governor lets go so the craft does not stay stuck.
create_stats.manual.page.flight_control_: Visual Flight Control Computer lesson. Use the sheet arrows, station chips, or numbered dots to step through the diagrams.
create_stats.manual.page.damage_observer: This block watches one named part of your ship or machine. Put it on a solid face. Open it and give the zone a name. Pick its role. Pick how big the watched area should be. Then use a Display Link to send that zone to a Battle Bridge.
create_stats.manual.page.battle_screen_d: This is the bridge that shows watched zones and weapon readiness. Put it on a wall. Use a Display Link from one or more Battle Observers into it. Then right-click the bridge. If it says there is no feed, check the Display Link first.
create_stats.manual.page.path_scanner.bo: This block looks at the ground ahead. Face it the way the vehicle should go. Let it scan loaded chunks. Then send its data with a Display Link to a Pathfinder Computer. The Scanner sees the world. It does not choose the path.
create_stats.manual.page.pathfinder_comp: This block picks a route from Scanner data. First link a Path Scanner into it with a Display Link. Then link its guidance to the FCC. When the scanner has fresh data, the Pathfinder Computer chooses a route and tells the FCC what direction to follow.
create_stats.manual.page.personal_reflec: Thank you for using Create Stats. If you run into any problems or have questions, you can reach me on Discord; the invite link is on the mod's Modrinth and CurseForge pages.
create_stats.manual.page.player_notes.bo: This space is for you. Write down what you've learned, your discoveries, troubleshooting lessons, and building tips. This is a small teaser for the upcoming Engineers Notebook item.
create_stats.ponder.kinetic_flywheel_ine: The Kinetic Flywheel banks rotational momentum at the end of a shaft
Drive it and it spools up, storing energy while it draws stress
A Display Link feeds live Charge %, Stored RPM, and mode to a Stats Display
When the engine stalls, the flywheel becomes the source and keeps the network turning
It coasts down on a friction curve, a mechanical UPS for windmill and engine dips
A comparator reads the charge as a 0-15 signal for low-reserve automation
On the panel: Arm or disarm discharge, Force Park, and set the low-reserve threshold
create_stats.ponder.rpm_governor_overvie: The RPM Governor is an inline actuator that sits along a kinetic line
Upstream kinetics drive its input side, just like any shaft
Until it is commanded the governor parks its output at zero; it is an actuator, not a pass-through gear
A Flight Control Computer claims it and commands an exact, signed output RPM
It drives the output branch to that RPM, independent of how fast the input turns
A negative command even spins the output the opposite way, reverse thrust on demand
If the FCC stops heart-beating the governor zeroes its output, a failsafe against runaway thrust
create_stats.ponder.smart_gearshift_gear: The Smart Gearshift is an inline gearbox that locks its output to an exact RPM
With no redstone signal it stays in Neutral and just hands the rotation through
Feed it a redstone signal of 1 to 15 and each level picks a fixed target RPM
A low gear throttles the output down to its target, even while the input races ahead
A high gear boosts it the other way, the output holds that exact RPM no matter the drive
A comparator reads back the active gear as a 0-15 signal for automation
create_stats.ponder.control_clutch_remot: The Control Clutch sits inline on a shaft and can break the drive on command
Engaged by default, it hands the full input speed to the output
Link it to a Factory Logic Controller, which can address many clutches by row
On a Stop command it disengages, the output halts while the input keeps turning
A Run command re-engages it and the output spins back up
The controller's 0-15 signal passes through to a comparator for downstream logic
If the controller stops responding the clutch safely defaults back to engaged
create_stats.ponder.induction_heater_kin: The Induction Heater is a stove that runs on rotation - no lava, no Blaze, just RPM
It only accepts power through its underside - run a shaft straight up into its base
At 64 RPM the plate idles Warm: a faint glow and gentle passive heat
128 RPM reaches Kindled: true cooking heat, billed to the network as 2048 SU
Goggles read the live tier, thermal charge, stress draw, and coil health at a glance
Slot in an Induction Coil and hold 256 RPM to go Superheated - the coil slowly burns away while it blazes, so keep spares in a hopper
A Basin or Boiler on top just works - the plate counts as a Blaze Burner, and Superheated counts as Seething
It is also literally a stove: right-click with raw food to lay a whole stack on the plate
All 64 share one timer and finish together - half the book time at Kindled, under a third when Superheated
Ding! Dinner stays on the plate for you or a hopper to collect - nothing is flung onto the floor
And mind your boots - the plate cannot tell chef from chicken at Kindled and above
create_stats.ponder.safety_clutch_stress: The Safety Clutch is a stress circuit-breaker wired inline on a shaft
While the network is healthy it stays engaged and drives the load
A comparator reports live network stress as a 0-15 signal
Cross the stress threshold, 80% by default, or overstress, and it instantly trips
Tripping disengages the output, sheltering your machines from overload
Once tripped it also emits a full redstone signal you can alarm or interlock on
Latch mode holds it open until you reset it; Auto-Reset retries after a few seconds
Reset it once stress settles and the drive smoothly resumes
create_stats.ponder.auto_transmission_cl: The Auto-Transmission Clutch is a self-tuning gearbox wired inline on a shaft
It constantly adjusts output speed to keep network stress inside a target band
A comparator reports the live stress reading, measured in SU or as a percentage
When stress sits below the band there is spare capacity, so it speeds the output up
When stress climbs past the band it eases the output down to protect the network
You set the stress band plus minimum and maximum RPM limits; it alarms if it cannot hold the floor
The result is hands-off throughput that always rides the edge of your stress budget
create_stats.ponder.load_balancer_twin_b: The Load Balancer takes one input shaft and feeds two separate output branches
Power arrives on the input face from a single source
By default it shares power evenly, a balanced 50/50 split across both branches
A comparator reports the live network stress as a 0-15 signal
Set the share to anything you like and it biases more speed onto the chosen branch
It also caps each branch to hold both sub-networks inside a stress band, with min and max RPM limits
One shaft in, two perfectly managed shafts out, no manual tuning required
create_stats.ponder.status_tower_light_o: The Status Tower Light is an at-a-glance operator beacon for any process
Point it at a metric, a local neighbour or a linked display target like this tank
While the reading stays healthy it glows steady green, all clear
Cross the warning threshold, 75% by default, and it switches to amber
At the critical threshold it turns red and emits a full redstone signal
Wire that signal to a horn, a shutdown, or a Safety Clutch to react automatically
When the process recovers it returns to green and the alarm clears on its own
create_stats.ponder.data_dial_wall_gauge: The Data Dial is a wall gauge that turns any reading into a sweeping analog needle
Read a local neighbour, or link it to a distant source like this tank
Live data wakes it up and the needle sweeps to the current value
Higher readings push the needle further round and shift its colour from cool to warm
Near full scale it glows hot, an instant visual warning across the room
The same reading is exported as a comparator signal from 0 to 15
Right-click to cycle which metric it tracks: speed, stress, fill, and more
create_stats.ponder.mini_display_paired_: The Mini Display is a compact wall screen that prints a live readout
Aim it at a source and the screen lights up with the value
It can track items, fluids, boiler heat, or kinetic speed and stress
Place a second screen right beside the first
The pair fuses into a single wide screen with room for longer labels and values
Right-click to choose the source and metric, or link it to a distant machine
Tidy at-a-glance readouts you can scatter across a whole factory wall
create_stats.ponder.holographic_projecto: The Holographic Projector beams a floating 3D data graph into the air above it
It scans neighbouring machines automatically, or you can link distant sources and display links
Live readings stream in and a translucent hologram blooms above the projector
Every sample is plotted over time, so rising or falling trends are obvious at a glance
Right-click for settings: switch between line and bar styles, colour themes, height and spin speed
It can also fire a redstone signal whenever a tracked value crosses a threshold you set
A dramatic, readable overview of your whole factory floating in mid-air
create_stats.ponder.battle_screen_displa: The Battle Screen is a tactical command console for your warships
Damage Observers watch each section of the hull and its weapons, then feed this console
Link them and a live battle hologram rises, green rings and pips mean all systems nominal
Take a hit and the hologram flares amber as sections report missing armour
Critical losses turn it red, so you read your fleet's condition at a glance
Right-click to open the tactical screen: aim and fire autocannons, enable auto-aim, or bind a linked controller
Repair the hull and the hologram returns to a calm, healthy green
create_stats.ponder.damage_observer_hull: The Damage Observer is a sentry that watches a structure for damage
Point it at a hull section and it scans the whole volume in front of it
Right-click to calibrate: it memorises every block as a healthy baseline
When blocks are blasted away it reports the missing count instantly and its lens turns red
It feeds live health and damage to Battle Screens and to displays through a display link
Repair the structure and the baseline is met again, back to a healthy green
create_stats.ponder.stats_recorder_data_: Stats Recorder: logging data over time
The Stats Recorder quietly logs any metric over time into its memory
Sit it next to a stats display, or wire it to a display link, and whatever they show becomes its source
Tick after tick it samples the value and keeps the whole history
Drop in a Memory Cog and it bottles up a snapshot of the recording you can carry away
Slot that cog into a display, or another recorder, to replay the exact data anywhere
It can auto-export to a CSV file, and a Signal Antenna lets it log machines from across your base
create_stats.ponder.calculator_working_c: The Calculator is a fully working calculator and function grapher built into a block
Its glowing face shows your expression and the result at a glance
Right-click to open the full screen, then type any expression, from simple sums to sin, cos, sqrt and powers
Switch to graph mode and plot functions of x as smooth curves over an adjustable range
Scientific mode, history, and pinned formulas keep your favourite equations one tap away
Place several together and they assemble into one big, high-resolution display
create_stats.ponder.factory_logic_contro: Factory Logic Controller: automate your factory
The Factory Logic Controller is a programmable brain for your whole factory
Its living screen tracks up to sixteen automation rules, each glowing with its status
Slot in Machine Selection Cards to choose exactly which machines each rule governs
Link Control or Safety Clutches with a link card and it starts and stops those machines for you, with no redstone wiring
Each rule watches its machines and runs them only while there is work to do. When they sit idle past your timeout, it stops them to save power
Right-click to open the editor and program every rule, then let your factory run itself
create_stats.ponder.freight_manifest_cli: Freight Manifest Clipboard: plan train cargo
The Freight Manifest Clipboard is a logistics planner for your whole train network
Hold it and right-click any Create Train Station to bind the clipboard to that depot
Right-click the placed clipboard to write a manifest: which goods, how many, and where they go
It turns each line into a delivery order, load or unload with a target amount, and validates every line before the schedule runs
Then it tracks live transfer progress as freight loads and unloads at the station
Pipe it into a Display Link or stats screen, and add a Signal Antenna to read distant stations
create_stats.ponder.overflow_gate_smart_: The Overflow Gate is a smart splitter that mounts on a belt and sorts the flow
By default items ride the belt straight through to your main line
Set a filter and the gate keeps filtered goods on the main route, filtered first, then anything else
When the main line is blocked, excess spills to the side belt you pick (left, forward, or right) after a short delay
Excess waits in the gate's buffer; sneak-use to collect it, or use it to read the live routing summary
create_stats.ponder.dispatch_board_stati: The Dispatch Board is a public live-ops display for a Create train station
Link it to a station and it shows the active train and every delivery order in real time
Each row is a cargo order, with the item, load or unload, and a live progress bar toward its target
The header tracks the train: arriving, loading, unloading, plus completed and remaining order counts
Stack boards into a wall for a big display, and add an antenna to monitor the station from afar
create_stats.ponder.vcc_overview.text_1: The engine spins, but the propeller stays parked until the VCC drives it
create_stats.ponder.vcc_overview.text_2: Tap the propeller with the Propeller Card
create_stats.ponder.vcc_overview.text_3: Tap its RPM Governor with the Governor Card
create_stats.ponder.vcc_overview.text_4: Drop both cards into the VCC, now they are a pair
create_stats.ponder.vcc_overview.text_5: Now the VCC spins that propeller for you
create_stats.ponder.vcc_overview.text_6: It sets the exact speed, forward or reverse, on command
create_stats.ponder.vcc_linked.header: VCC Linked Mode: pair with Redstone Links
create_stats.ponder.vcc_linked.text_1: Not every device wants a card, some pair by Redstone Link
create_stats.ponder.vcc_linked.text_2: Set a Redstone Link on the burner and choose a frequency
create_stats.ponder.vcc_linked.text_3: Drop a matching Link into the VCC, same frequency, now they are paired
create_stats.ponder.vcc_linked.text_4: The VCC throttles the burner by radio, a clean 0 to 15 signal
create_stats.ponder.vcc_linked.text_5: Or a Linked Controller drives those links from across the build
create_stats.ponder.vcc_linked.text_6: Heat builds and the whole craft lifts, linked, never carded
create_stats.ponder.vcc_linked.text_7: Ease the command down and the link relaxes the burner; it settles to a hover
create_stats.ponder.pathfinder_computer_: The Pathfinder Computer plans a safe route across the world for a Create vehicle
Link a Path Scanner and it reads the terrain, the input port lights up and the planner gets to work
It explores thousands of cells, weighing slopes, gaps and hazards to find the cheapest safe path
When a route is found the screen draws it with a confidence score and total distance
Link a Flight Control Computer and the output port goes green, the route is handed over to be driven
If the terrain is blocked or the search budget runs out it shows a broken route and keeps the last good one
create_stats.ponder.path_scanner_terrain: The Path Scanner turns the world around it into a navigation grid for vehicles
It reads the chunks in front of it, classifying every cell as passable, marginal or blocked
Once a region is fully loaded the lens glows and the coverage bar fills, the map is ready
Cells it cannot see yet stay unknown, the amber bar shows the gaps until those chunks load
Link it to a Pathfinder Computer and this grid becomes the map the route planner searches
Tune the scan radius and chunk budget to balance coverage against performance
create_stats.ponder.stats_alarm_threshol: The Stats Alarm watches the channels on a nearby Stats Display Panel and reacts the moment one of them goes into alert
It only needs to sit near the panel, add an antenna to stretch its watch range across larger builds
Its side face is a redstone source, wire the output to lamps, doors or contraptions
When a watched channel trips its limit it lights up, sounds an alarm and emits a full redstone signal
As soon as that channel leaves its alert range the alarm clears itself automatically
Pick its alarm sound, particles and whether it drives redstone; the above or below limit itself is set on the panel's channel
create_stats.ponder.table_alarm_clock_al: A desk clock for your base: alarm, countdown timer, stopwatch and a shared calendar
Right-click to open it and set an alarm time, a countdown, or start the stopwatch
Its side face is a redstone source, hook it up to wake your machines on schedule
When the time comes it rings, lights up and powers its redstone output until you stop it
Sneak right-click to silence it, the ring and the redstone signal switch off
Switch to Calendar mode to plan dated events and invite other players by name; the schedule is saved on the server
create_stats.ponder.stats_display_gettin: The Stats Display is a wall panel that turns live machine data into a readout
Place panels with the same facing side by side and they merge into one big screen
A Display Link carries data from a source to the panel. Click the panel, then the source
Right-click the panel to open Home; sneak-right-click cycles the small in-world view
Blank panel? Make sure the link sits on the source, then pick Stats Link in that source's menu
create_stats.ponder.stats_display_readin: Open Home: every linked block becomes a source card, grouped by family
Storage, fluids, and kinetics each expose their own channels
A channel is one metric from one source: RPM, fill, item count, heat, or status
Line, bar, gauge, numeric, and capacity views read the same channel differently
Output mode sets the goal: Single Channel, Dashboard, Specialized diagram, or Analog
Use time range and autoscale for trends; hide noisy channels before you build a board
create_stats.ponder.stats_display_dashbo: Some data reads best as a page: Inventory Status, Factory Status, Topology, and Train Map
When a family has a built-in board, open that page before hand-tuning graph settings
create_stats.ponder.stats_display_create: Stressometers and Speedometers become kinetic cards with live RPM and stress capacity
Chests, vaults, belts, and tanks turn into fill and capacity readouts
Safety, Auto-Transmission, and Control Clutches report why a branch is held or released
Load Balancers and Mini Displays can become control cards, not just charts
Reach for Factory Controls and Factory Status when the question is operational
create_stats.ponder.stats_display_diesel: Diesel Telemetry
Bind a Diesel Engine: single, modular, huge, or a whole engine group
Bind the fuel tank too: the engine page shows NO LINK without its reserve
Distillation pages show crude input, heat, and the diesel or gasoline output lanes
Pumpjacks, burners, and tanks explain why a process is starved or backed up
After binding, pick the engine source and choose Specialized for the full diagram
create_stats.ponder.stats_display_vehicl: A Vehicle Control Center feeds the Aero Flight Deck: propulsion, attitude, altitude, sensors
Aeroline Director adds route, heading, approach, and guidance for the same craft
Train Stations, Dispatch Boards, and Freight Manifests are your logistics sources
Station data unlocks the Train Map; cargo sources show lines, orders, and history
When station data is live, read the Train Map before chasing individual cargo channels
create_stats.ponder.stats_display_combat: Battle Observers scan a ship and tag every block as present, lost, or newly added
A Battle Bridge gathers those scans into one combat source for the panel
The board then shows integrity, lost-block composition, cargo state, and weapon readiness
The Configurator copies, pastes, and edits panel layouts in place
The Handheld opens any linked display from a distance
Recorder stores snapshots, Projector mirrors a panel elsewhere, Alarms react to thresholds
create_stats.ponder.stats_display_battle: Battle Observers scan the ship and tag every block as present, lost, or newly added
A Battle Bridge gathers those scans into one combat source for the panel
Set that source to Tactical mode to build a live 3D reconstruction of the hull
Drag to orbit, right-click to freeze, and use the Y slider to peel away upper decks
The 2D / 3D switch flips between the flat integrity console and the rotatable hull
Integrity, lost-block composition, and weapon readiness keep updating as the battle unfolds
block.create_stats.open_frame_dynamo.too: Converts shaft rotation into Forge Energy. The frugal grade.
Drive the shaft on its bottom face; energy leaves every other face.
270 FE/t at 256 RPM for 8192 SU. Least output of the three and by far the best value: 0.033 FE per stress unit, half again what the Kinetic Dynamo manages.
Build this when rotation is the thing you are short of. Two of these produce 540 FE/t on the same 16384 SU one Kinetic Dynamo spends on 360.
block.create_stats.industrial_alternator: Converts shaft rotation into Forge Energy. The dense grade.
Drive the shaft on its bottom face; energy leaves every other face.
540 FE/t at 256 RPM for 19661 SU. Half again the output of a Kinetic Dynamo from one block, at 0.0275 FE per stress unit.
Build this when floor space is the thing you are short of. It is not the efficient one; it is the one that fits.
block.create_stats.induction_range.toolt: An electric hob. Forge Energy in, heat out, at the setting you choose.
Wire it with Surface Cable or a Power Connector. The control panel faces you when placed.

Right click to turn the dial: off, Low 16 FE/t, Medium 64 FE/t, High 256 FE/t. Low cooks like a campfire, Medium also smelts, High also blasts. Belts and funnels load and unload it, and a funnel only ever pulls a finished batch.

Medium is Create Heated and High is Superheated, matching a fuelled Blaze Burner and a blaze cake exactly, so Basins and Boilers behave as they would on one. A range also powers every range within one block of it, so a 3x3 bank runs off a single cable landing anywhere on its edge.
create_stats.ponder.cable_grades.text_1: Surface Cable lies on block faces and turns corners, for wiring that stays inside a build rather than hanging across it
create_stats.ponder.cable_grades.text_2: Click to start a run, aim where it should go to preview it, then click again to lay it. Click a machine to finish on it
create_stats.ponder.cable_grades.text_3: Sneak while running to stop there, or sneak on a finished run to pull all of it back into your pocket
create_stats.ponder.cable_grades.text_4: Three grades: Surface Cable at the base rate, Cable Tray at three times it, and Bus Duct at six
create_stats.ponder.cable_grades.text_5: Width is the readout. A heavier grade is drawn visibly fatter, so you can tell a trunk from a spur across a room without opening anything
create_stats.ponder.cable_grades.text_6: It carries more, not sooner. The grid is solved whole every tick, so power already reaches the far end of any run immediately
create_stats.ponder.cable_grades.text_7: Spend the Bus Duct on the run between your generators and your distribution panel, where everything else has to fit through
create_stats.ponder.cable_grades.text_8: One cable block carries one circuit. Two circuits down one corridor means two cables side by side, exactly as a real install looks
create_stats.ponder.cable_grades.text_9: Dye is how you tell them apart: colour is the circuit, so two runs of different colours can share a wall without joining
create_stats.ponder.cable_rated_hops.hea: Connectors and wire: rating a hop
create_stats.ponder.cable_rated_hops.tex: A hop through open air is made of three rated parts: the terminal at each end, and the wire strung between them
Copper Wire moves the base rate, Insulated Wire twice it, and Shielded Wire three times
The Advanced Power Connector is the same terminal rated for three times the throughput, and mounts exactly like the plain one
Here is the rule that catches people out: a hop only moves as much as its weakest part
Two Advanced connectors joined by plain Copper Wire still move the base rate. The upgrade is wasted until the wire matches
Upgrade both ends and the wire between them and the hop finally carries three times the base rate
The base rate, and every multiplier above it, is tunable in the [power.wiring] config section
create_stats.ponder.fe_electric_drive.te: The Electric Drive is the exact inverse of the Kinetic Dynamo: energy in, rotation out
It is its own Power Connector. Do not mount one on top: the wire lands on the two studs of the terminal box on the machine itself
The shaft comes out of the face it points at, and the Drive is a kinetic source: it provides both a speed and a stress capacity
MK I sources 128 RPM with 4,096 stress units behind it, for 512 energy a tick
MK II sources 256 RPM, Create's top speed, with 16,384 units for 1,024 a tick. Both cost the same four energy per RPM
So the bill scales with the speed you asked for and nothing else. You are never punished for building the bigger grade
Feeding a Drive's shaft into a dynamo always loses energy. It moves power across the kinetic world; it never mints it
Redstone is a cut-out, as it is everywhere else in the power system, and a Distribution Unit can shed a Drive like any other load
create_stats.ponder.fe_fluid_pump.header: FE Fluid Pump: pressure you dial
create_stats.ponder.fe_fluid_pump.text_1: The FE Fluid Pump is a pipe segment that drives fluid along its run, pulling in through the back and pushing out of the front
create_stats.ponder.fe_fluid_pump.text_2: Like the Electric Drive it is its own Power Connector: wire straight to the studs on its terminal box, with no connector block on top
create_stats.ponder.fe_fluid_pump.text_3: Scroll the power dial to choose the flow you want in millibuckets a tick. It costs energy per millibucket actually moved
create_stats.ponder.fe_fluid_pump.text_4: Dialling it down is a real saving rather than a throttle, because a pump that is asked for less is charged for less
create_stats.ponder.fe_fluid_pump.text_5: MK I tops out at 64 millibuckets a tick, exactly a Create pump spun at 128 RPM. MK II reaches 128, matching Create's top speed
create_stats.ponder.fe_fluid_pump.text_6: Pinning the grades to numbers you already know from Create is what makes the throughput mean something
create_stats.ponder.fe_fluid_pump.text_7: Splice a Flow Meter into the same run to see what the dial is actually achieving downstream
create_stats.ponder.induction_range.head: Induction Range: an electric hob
create_stats.ponder.induction_range.text: The Induction Range is an electric hob: energy in, heat out, at whichever of three settings you dial
Feed it with Surface Cable or a Power Connector, and it is placed with its control panel facing you rather than into the wall
Right-click to turn the dial. Low costs 16 energy a tick and cooks like a campfire, Medium 64 and also smelts, High 256 and also blasts
Medium is exactly Create's Heated and High exactly Superheated, so a Basin or a Boiler behaves as it would on a Blaze Burner or a blaze cake
A range also powers every range within one block of it, so a three by three bank runs off a single cable landing anywhere on its edge
Belts and funnels load and unload it, and a funnel only ever pulls a finished batch rather than half-cooked items
If the grid cannot hold the setting you asked for, the range says so rather than quietly dropping a level. That is your cue to look at the generators
create_stats.ponder.flow_meter_reading.t: The Flow Meter is a length of pipe that counts what goes through it. Fluid moves exactly as it would through copper pipe
Splice it into a line and it auto-aligns with whatever pipe or tank it finds beside it. It can be waterlogged like any pipe
Point a Display Link from the meter at a Stats Display and the readings become a panel you can read across a room
It reports four things: which fluid, which way it is going, the rate in millibuckets a tick, and the total volume moved so far
Switch the panel to Specialized mode for an animated pipe with a flow gauge and a direction arrow
Set a redstone trigger from that panel and the meter emits a signal while fluid is flowing, or when the rate crosses a number you pick
One reading that surprises people: if the tank in front is full the fluid cannot move, so the meter correctly reads idle while the pump keeps pushing
create_stats.ponder.lamp_fittings.text_1: Six fittings share one behaviour and differ only in shape and brightness, so you can light a room in the style it deserves
create_stats.ponder.lamp_fittings.text_2: The High Bay and the Panel reach full daylight, the Caged Bulkhead and Strip sit just under, and the Dome and Sconce are softer
create_stats.ponder.lamp_fittings.text_3: Every fitting mounts on any face and points away from whatever you clicked, so the same lamp works on a ceiling, a wall or a floor
create_stats.ponder.lamp_fittings.text_4: Right-click a fitting with any dye to recolour it. All sixteen colours work, and no menu is involved
create_stats.ponder.lamp_fittings.text_5: Colour is per fitting, so one run of cable can carry a whole scheme rather than a single tint
create_stats.ponder.lamp_circuits.text_1: A fitting with nothing feeding it is simply a dark fitting. Lamps run on cable power whether or not FE Dependent Mode is switched on
create_stats.ponder.lamp_circuits.text_2: Surface Cable lies on block faces and turns corners. Click to start a run, aim to preview it, click again to lay it
create_stats.ponder.lamp_circuits.text_3: Each fitting is a piece of the circuit, not just something hanging off it, so the run carries on through each housing into the next
create_stats.ponder.lamp_circuits.text_4: That is why one cable landing anywhere on a row lights the whole row. A lamp costs one energy a tick, so a single alternator carries hundreds
create_stats.ponder.lamp_circuits.text_5: Dye the cable too: colour is the circuit, so two runs of different colours can share a wall without joining
create_stats.ponder.lamp_circuits.text_6: A Switch Link Card pairs a switch to fittings it is not wired to. Click the switch to hold it, then click lamps
create_stats.ponder.lamp_circuits.text_7: A linked lamp is still being fed. The switch only decides whether it lights, which is what lets one plate control a room it is nowhere near
create_stats.ponder.lamp_circuits.text_8: Redstone is the third way, and it works backwards from vanilla: a signal force-kills a fitting rather than lighting it
create_stats.ponder.lamp_circuits.text_9: That keeps redstone from becoming a second way to power a lamp, so vanilla logic can sit on top of the wiring without replacing it
create_stats.ponder.lamp_circuits.text_1: The third is the supply itself. Each fitting holds a few seconds in reserve, so a dip as machines start up never shows as a flicker
Drain it for real and you get this instead: the fittings sag, flicker, and go out. A flickering room means look at your generators
create_stats.ponder.stage_light_aiming.t: The Stage Light is a moving-head spotlight. Unlike the fixed fittings it aims wherever you point it, on any mounting face
Right-click it for the aiming panel: a pan compass and a tilt slider, with a live preview of where the beam lands
Range sets how far it throws, brightness how hard, and focus tightens it from a wide flood to a narrow spot
Beam width and light spread are separate on purpose: the visible cone and the light it actually casts can be sized independently
Slot stained glass as a beam filter to tint it, exactly like a gel in front of a real lantern
Strobe, pulse and rainbow effects run on a speed you set, and redstone can aim the head as well as the panel can
One caveat worth knowing before you build: a light mounted on a moving contraption needs LambDynamicLights installed to actually shine
create_stats.ponder.stage_light_mk2_reac: Stage Light MK II: reach and upgrade
The MK II is the same lantern in gold, with every control the original has and double the reach at 128 blocks
Right-click it with a Beacon to slot a range upgrade and double it again, out to 256 blocks
A wrench pops the Beacon back out, so the upgrade is a loan rather than a one-way craft
That reach is what makes it a floodlight for an airship or a quarry rather than a room light. At close range the original is the cheaper choice
create_stats.ponder.stats_display_mk2.he: Stats Display Mk II: the studio
create_stats.ponder.stats_display_mk2.te: The Stats Display Mk II is the same panel with a full-screen configuration studio behind it
Everything you already know carries over: matching panels placed side by side with the same facing merge into one larger screen
It reads exactly the same sources through exactly the same Display Links, so a Mk I wall can be upgraded panel by panel
Right-click opens the studio instead of the old screen. Sneak-right-click still cycles the small in-world view
The eight Stats Display chapters cover sources, channels, dashboards and the specialized diagrams. All of them apply here unchanged
create_stats.ponder.vcc_mk2.header: VCC Mk II: the flight deck so far
create_stats.ponder.vcc_mk2.text_1: The VCC Mk II is a gold-cased cockpit console with a live CRT flight deck drawn on its screen
create_stats.ponder.vcc_mk2.text_2: Place it on a Sable contraption and the screen shows a glass-cockpit readout of the craft it is riding
create_stats.ponder.vcc_mk2.text_3: Right-click with an empty hand to cycle the screen state, so you can see all four CRT themes in place before you commit to a cockpit layout
create_stats.ponder.vcc_mk2.text_4: Worth knowing before you build around it: this is a look-first milestone. The full control interface is still being built
create_stats.ponder.vcc_mk2.text_5: It is also a separate system from the Flight Control Computer rather than a replacement for it, so the FCC's controls are not hiding in here
create_stats.ponder.fe_power_basics.head: Forge Energy: generating and wiring
create_stats.ponder.fe_power_basics.text: The Kinetic Dynamo turns rotation into Forge Energy. Drive its bottom shaft and it generates energy per tick in proportion to speed
Faster rotation makes more power, and costs more stress. It works whether or not FE Dependent Mode is on, so it can feed other FE mods too
Mount a Power Connector on anything that makes or uses power. It reads whatever block it is attached to
Right-click one connector with Copper Wire, then a second, to span a cable between them
Every connected connector forms one grid, solved as a whole each tick, so power reaches the far end immediately no matter how long the run is
Machines are always served before storage, and when supply runs short the grid splits it fairly rather than letting the first machine drink it all
create_stats.ponder.fe_dynamo_grades.tex: The Kinetic Dynamo is the baseline every figure is quoted against: 360 energy a tick at Create's top speed
That is deliberately equal to a Crafts and Additions alternator, on stress as well as on output, so the number means something
The Industrial Alternator makes half again as much, 540 a tick, and eats more stress to do it
The Open Frame Dynamo makes the least, 270 a tick, but takes only half the stress of the baseline
So these are not a ladder. The axis that matters is energy per unit of stress, and the cheapest grade wins it outright
Rotation to spare and no room to build? Take the Industrial. Windmills already groaning? A row of Open Frames gets more out of the same stress
All three scale with speed, so a dynamo spun at half its rated RPM makes half the power. The base level is tunable in the [power.generator] config
create_stats.ponder.fe_capacitor_bank.te: A Capacitor Bank stores Forge Energy and shows its charge on the outside
Touching banks merge into one battery, so a stack needs a single connector rather than one per block
Merging pays a bonus: the pool holds more than the blocks would separately, so building bigger is worth it
It fills from the bottom block upward and drains from the top down, so the stack reads as one big gauge
Lit blocks are charge and dark blocks are headroom, readable across a base without opening anything
create_stats.ponder.fe_dependent_mode.he: FE Dependent Mode: brownout and cutoff
create_stats.ponder.fe_dependent_mode.te: FE Dependent Mode is optional and off by default. Switch it on and the mod's electronics each need power to run
Every powered block keeps a small internal buffer that any grid can charge. Simple gauges and kinetic blocks never need it
Cut the supply and the buffer drains. Below a fifth the block browns out and its screens start to flicker
When the buffer empties the block goes inert. It stops working but keeps its settings
Power it again and it charges like a capacitor before restarting, so a marginal supply cannot make it flicker on and off
Every buffer, drain and the restart threshold are tunable in the [power] config section
create_stats.ponder.fe_power_distributio: Without a Power Distribution Unit a short grid splits power evenly, so every machine browns out together and you lose all of them
Power goes in through either side boss. Everything the panel can hand out comes from what your generators are actually making
Run a Copper Wire from one of the eight studs on top to a machine's connector, and that machine is on that leg
Right-click the panel and sort your machines into five tiers, from Critical down to Optional
The flight computer is Critical, the readouts are High, the pump is Medium, and the decorative light is Optional
While generation covers the whole demand the panel does nothing at all. Every leg is served and the bar above it stays full
create_stats.ponder.fe_pdu_active_auto.t: The panel has three modes. Off shares power evenly, Manual honours your tiers, and Active Auto manages the branch for you
In Manual the reserve is what tells the panel anything is wrong, and a reserve only reports a shortfall once it is already draining
So the whole branch coasts on stored energy, and by the time the panel reacts the reserve you were saving for an outage is spent
Active Auto measures what your dynamos can actually generate, rather than waiting for the buffer to run down
It sheds on the way down instead of after the fall, so the reserve is never touched at all
The buffer stops being the sensor and becomes what it should be: a reserve, held back so Critical keeps running through an outage
create_stats.ponder.switch_plates.header: Switches: the set and the signal
create_stats.ponder.switch_plates.text_1: Five plates that all mount flush on a wall, floor or ceiling, and all point away from the face you clicked
create_stats.ponder.switch_plates.text_2: Every one of them latches: it stays where you put it and reads on or off from across a room, the push button included
create_stats.ponder.switch_plates.text_3: The Isolator is the chunky lockable rotary you put on the wall beside a machine. Its handle turns a quarter turn when thrown
create_stats.ponder.switch_plates.text_4: They emit redstone the way a lever does: weakly to everything around them, and strongly into the block they are mounted on
create_stats.ponder.switch_plates.text_5: So a switch on a wall drives whatever is on the other side of that wall, which is the whole reason to put one there
create_stats.ponder.switch_plates.text_6: The Double Switch is two independent switches sharing one plate. Click the left half or the right half and only that gang moves
create_stats.ponder.switch_plates.text_7: Each gang powers its own side of the block so it can drive two circuits, and both still feed the block behind
create_stats.ponder.switch_circuits.head: Switches: breaking the run
create_stats.ponder.switch_circuits.text: A switch is not a signal on the side of a circuit. It is a link in the run itself, wired in line like the real thing
Open it and the contacts part. Everything downstream is cut off from the supply and goes dark, however long the run is
The half in front of the switch is still live. It is the circuit that is broken, not the power
Close it and both halves rediscover each other on the same tick, so the room comes back immediately rather than on the next block update
When you cannot run cable through the switch, a Switch Link Card pairs it to fittings instead. Click the switch to hold it, then click lamps
A linked lamp is still fed by its own cable. The switch only tells it whether to light, so one plate can control a room it is nowhere near
Sneak-click to let go of the held switch, and click a linked lamp again to unlink it
create_stats.ponder.fe_power_distributio: Slow the generators and the budget shrinks. The panel drops the bottom tier first: the lights go, and nothing else notices
Starve it further and Medium goes too. Each tier coasts on its own reserve on the way down, so shedding is soft rather than a blackout
What is left goes upward. Critical is still running on a grid that can no longer light a lamp
Bring the generators back and the tiers return in the order they matter, so the room recovers instead of stampeding
You keep your flight computer and lose the decorative lights, instead of losing everything at once
create_stats.ponder.fe_pdu_active_auto.t: Within a tier it sheds the hungriest machine first, so the most of your build keeps running for the power you have
Right-click a machine in the list to lock it on so it is never shed, or off so it never runs. A lock overrules the panel entirely
